title: Mac/PC trials.log split understates the multiple-testing count
detail: Every trials.log row before 2026-05-05 exists only on the Mac file. The 2026-06 gate recalibration and gate-spec-v2 family variance/N were computed on the incomplete PC file, so N is understated for every DSR haircut derived from it. Decide: merge the Mac pre-2026-05-05 rows, or document the two-machine split as a permanent asterisk on every N-based statistic. trials.log is a sacred-harness file, so the merge itself is human-only.

title: Pre-Phase-4.E trials are fee-optimistic (0.04% vs a real 0.10% taker)
detail: Every trial before Phase 4.E used simulator defaults FEE_MARKET=0.04% (a Binance FUTURES taker rate) plus 0.05% slippage, on a SPOT substrate whose real taker fee is 0.10%. High-turnover rows (CrossSectionalReversal 1432 trades, NewsSentimentMomentum 2071 trades) are the most affected. Recorded as a caveat in docs/validation_framework.md under Gate spec v2; re-check at 0.10% before any of those rows is cited as evidence.

title: Formally park NewsSentimentMomentum and AttentionMomentum (holdout regen not worth it)
detail: Both sit 7-10 months below the MinTRL floor and land at SR ~0.75 even if extended, below the 52-month floor of 0.79. Extending either needs a holdout regeneration, which is human-only and shrinks the virgin window for every other strategy. research_revival_2026-09 section A.4 recommends NOT regenerating. Open rather than resolved because no human decision has been recorded.

title: Binance UM data caveats must be honoured by every perp design
detail: Three caveats from the recon: (1) sum_open_interest drops to a hard 0 for ~10 hours per symbol, a feed glitch, so any 24h-OI-change feature must mask or repair those hours or it manufactures spurious collapse events; (2) alt OI / long-short / taker-ratio metrics only start 2021-12, so a cross-sectional OI study before that is BTC-only; (3) funding_interval_hours is NOT always 8h (5 symbols at 2h, 4 at 4h, heaviest around Nov 2022 near the FTX collapse), so a funding-carry design must read the interval per settlement.

title: Six kept bash hooks still depend on jq and are silently inert
detail: The 2026-09-02 governance port replaced the seven SECURITY hooks with Python. Six advisory/observability hooks were kept as bash and still shell out to jq, which is not installed on this machine: failcount-check.sh, failcount-update.sh, flush-T1.sh, run-tests-fast.sh, budget-check.sh, exit-ramp-check.sh. They exit 127 and do nothing. They gate nothing security-relevant, so they were out of scope for the port, but 'the hook is wired' currently means less than it reads. Port them to Python or install jq.

title: architecture.md C.1 phase5-coordinator hooks row contradicts the D8 implementation
detail: The C.1 row reads 'Same as phase4b-coord', which would include the PostToolUse failcount-update hook. Commit 6733131 deliberately drops it because Phase 5 sessions are atomic fan-outs, not a sequential variation loop. Either spell out the divergence in C.1 or add a footnote; pick at the next architecture.md edit. Settled in chat 2026-05-03.
surfaced_in: docs/open_questions.md '[OPEN, 2026-05-03] architecture.md C.1 phase5-coordinator hooks row'

title: TradeRecord.entry_time records wall-clock, not the candle timestamp
detail: paper_trading/simulator.py:107-108 sets entry_time/exit_time to datetime.now() at the moment the simulator processes the trade, not the historical bar. Any retrospective trade-time analysis consuming TradeRecord.entry_time directly is wrong; it surfaced when bucketing DualMomentum's 44 dev trades put all of them in one wall-clock instant. Needs the candle timestamp threaded through execute_signal into _handle_buy / _handle_full_sell.

title: Phase 4 deployment mechanics undecided (fresh state vs parallel)
detail: Deploy to the existing server with fresh 100k paper state, or preserve the current paper state and deploy in parallel for comparison? Needed before any Phase 4.F strategy reaches paper deploy (megaloop stage S6).

title: Checkpoint balance mismatch on the server
detail: The '100k Apr 17 fresh' balances in the server checkpoint do not match the bot's internal state. Needs reproduction from logs and a deliberate reset.

title: portfolio/manager.py module docstring names the wrong slot count and phase letters
detail: manager.py lines 1-19 say 'StrategySlot x 6' and 'Phase D + E combined'. Both are pre-OKX-migration phase letters and the wrong slot count (the portfolio is 10 strategies). Cosmetic; batch it with the next manager.py edit. manager.py is Tier 2 schema-stable, so a docstring-only change is contract-preserving and agent-autonomous.

title: no-secrets-in-bash.py Resend pattern false-positives on p-r-e_ prefixed paths
detail: The Resend key pattern re_[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{20,} has no left boundary, so it matches INSIDE the path scripts/p<r>e_commit_backlog_check.sh (the 20 characters after 're_' are 'commit_backlog_check'). Any Bash command naming that script is blocked. Fix: anchor the pattern as (?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])re_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,} . Blocked from self-fixing: .claude/hooks/*.py is Tier 1 and this session has no SACRED_OVERRIDE_FILES. Commits are unaffected (the git hook calls the script from inside git, not through a Bash tool call); only typing the path is blocked.

title: schemas/agent_frontmatter.schema.json still carries siamese's required list
detail: The file was copied verbatim from siamese-reconcile and requires agent_id / version / model_rationale, which no crypto-bot agent carries; its 'model' enum also omits 'inherit', which three cross-model agents use deliberately. scripts/validate_agent_frontmatter.py was re-fitted to crypto-bot's real contract and passes 21/21, but only in its default built-in mode — running it with --schema would fail every file. Fix the schema's required list, description and model enum to match the validator. Blocked from self-fixing: schemas/*.schema.json is Tier 1 and this session has no SACRED_OVERRIDE_FILES.

title: Megaloop stages S1.6 and S2-S7 are blocked: no SACRED_OVERRIDE_FILES in a desktop session
detail: path-allowlist.py reads its pre-authorization from the SACRED_OVERRIDE_FILES env var of its OWN process, which it inherits from the Claude Code process. This session was not started from the prompt's Git Bash launch line, so the var is unset and every Tier 1 path is blocked even though the prompt's AUTONOMY block pre-authorizes them. An agent cannot set it from inside the session, and must not (self-granting authority). Remaining blocked work: S1.6 docs/architecture.md section E; S2 backtest/holdout_manifest.json + backtest/holdout.py, which gates S3-S7 entirely. Unblock by relaunching with the launch line in docs/megaloop_prompt_2026-09-02.md.

title: no-secrets-in-bash.py Resend pattern false-positives on paths containing 're_'
detail: FIXED. Pattern narrowed to (?<![A-Za-z0-9_-])re_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,} : a left lookbehind so it cannot match mid-token, and an alnum-only body because real Resend keys are base62. Pinned by four fixtures in eval/fixtures/hooks/hook-regressions-2026-09.jsonl, including one proving a real key still blocks -- the fix narrowed the pattern, it did not delete it.
closed_in: megaloop 2026-09-02, S1 follow-up after owner authorization

title: schemas/agent_frontmatter.schema.json still carried siamese's required list
detail: FIXED. required[] now matches crypto-bot's real contract (name/description/model/tools/permissionMode/maxTurns/memory); the model enum admits 'inherit' for the three cross-model agents. jsonschema IS installed here, so --schema now runs a real draft-07 pass: 21/21 valid in both modes.

title: commit-guard.py treated any command mentioning 'git commit' as a commit
detail: FIXED. The invocation test was a regex over the raw command, so a python heredoc whose SOURCE quoted a git-commit command was validated as if its python body were a commit message, and refused. Now: strip heredoc bodies, tokenize into pipeline segments, require argv0 == git with the first non-flag argument == commit, and keep scanning later segments so `git add -A && git commit` is still gated. Seven fixtures pin it. Same failure class as BK-0011: a guard that false-blocks routine work gets disabled by whoever hits it, which is a slower way of failing open.
closed_in: megaloop 2026-09-02, S1 follow-up after owner authorization

title: Tier 1 writes need SACRED_OVERRIDE_FILES, which a desktop session does not inherit
detail: UNBLOCKED 2026-09-02 by explicit owner authorization in chat ('I authorize it you can fix any file you needed to'). The grant is carried to the hook through an env block in .claude/settings.local.json, which Claude Code injects into the session and which propagates to hook subprocesses mid-session (verified empirically). settings.local.json is untracked, so the grant is machine-local. STILL OPEN because that env block MUST be removed at the end of the run: left in place it silently disarms the Tier 1 guard for every future session on this machine, which is strictly worse than the launch-line mechanism it stands in for. The durable fix is to use the megaloop launch line; see docs/handoff_template.md.

title: Phase 4.F closed 0/3 UNTESTABLE - decide direction on the perp substrate
detail: All three C.4 families closed as untestable, not killed: MDE exceeded the pre-registered threshold in every case and widening is exhausted. The Binance UM discovery window is too small to resolve structural effects at the 1.5-3% scale. Options for a human: (a) accept the A.6 overlay as the standing deliverable and stop perp research; (b) re-pre-register the families at effect sizes the window CAN resolve, accepting they are then different claims; (c) move the statistical weight to the confirmation window, which changes the discovery/confirmation split's purpose. Not blocking anything; nothing runs until this is decided.

title: LEAD: 1-day CONTINUATION after OI-collapse cascades (opposite sign to the reversal hypothesis)
detail: deleveraging_reversal at +1 day: mean -6.28%, t=-7.78, N=220, MDE 2.42% -- large, significant and adequately powered, unlike the pre-registered +3 day headline. Sign is inverted: price CONTINUES after a 20% OI collapse plus a 2-sigma move. NOT acted on and must not be: it is not the pre-registered statistic, and adopting a horizon because its number looked better is the substitution the discovery/confirmation split forbids. Testing it properly = a new pre-registered screen, threshold frozen first, N_disc becomes 2 for the family. Caveat that travels with it: entry is at the close of a >=2-sigma cascade day when spreads are widest and depth thinnest, against a cost model calibrated to normal conditions -- it may be real and untradeable.

title: Overlay drawdown result rests on a single 2022 episode and a favourable window
detail: The A.6 overlay reports a 79% relative drawdown reduction, better than the QuantPedia practitioner benchmark of roughly halved. Treat the gap as a warning: the window (2021-05-30..2025-05-01) contains exactly ONE major decline, and it excludes March 2020 -- the sharp V-shaped crash case that trend overlays handle WORST, where they exit after the fall and re-enter after the recovery. The window is by accident favourable to the rule. Effective sample size for the headline metric is one. Re-score if earlier BTC/ETH spot data is ever cached.
